claims.statement: The definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026, and importers above a 50-tonne mass threshold must obtain authorised CBAM declarant status.
Accredited verifiers can issue the first verification reports in 2027 and declarants finalise 2026 declarations in September 2027.
Demand hypothesis: mid-market importers will outsource supplier evidence reconciliation because customs records, foreign installation data and verifier requirements meet only at the annual close.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes many small importers from scope.
Customs, carbon-accounting and ERP incumbents are rapidly adding CBAM modules.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: customs brokers identify threshold-crossing importers and bundle the close workflow
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 250 importers averaging 50000 PLN annual recurring revenue could exceed 12m PLN ARR; trusted broker and verifier workflows could support founder equity above 5m PLN in 4-6 years
economics.founder_time: 16-22 hours weekly with emissions-accounting review contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 65-82% blended margin as complex supplier exceptions require analysts
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 9-15 months with twelve recurring importers
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 15000-50000 PLN annual subscription plus 10000-40000 PLN per close and supplier fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monthly imports, new suppliers and mandatory annual declarations and verification

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned supplier-installation mappings, commodity classifications and prior close lineage reduce repeat reconciliation effort
fingerprint.customer: EU mid-market importers of steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, electricity or hydrogen above the CBAM threshold
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded into customs-broker classification and import-account workflows
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier evidence portal, shipment reconciliation and verifier-ready close workspace sold through customs brokers
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays annual platform fee, supplier onboarding and year-end close fee
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Imports cross the threshold or the annual CBAM close approaches with incomplete foreign-supplier emissions data

founder_fit: Quantitative emissions reconciliation matches data-science and finance interests
Annual-close automation can be built part-time in one commodity
Broker-led acquisition reduces continuous social selling
risks: Foreign suppliers may not provide verifiable installation data.
Errors affect certificate costs and regulatory exposure.
Broker concentration could create channel dependence.

structure.control_point: The evidence-complete annual dataset released to an accredited verifier and declarant
structure.critical_dependency: Foreign supplier cooperation, accurate customs data and accredited verifier acceptance

thesis: A customs-broker-embedded close workflow could collect installation-level emissions evidence, reconcile commodity and shipment data, maintain authorised-declarant readiness and assemble the annual verification packet for importers just above the mass threshold. Accredited verifiers retain verification authority. Demand and economics are hypotheses.
title: CBAM Supplier-Evidence Close for Mid-Market Importers
uncertainties: Count of Polish importers just above threshold
Verifier acceptance of generated evidence packets
Importer willingness to pay before first close
